new_findings.finding: An unavailable Web Locks API is rendered as a retryable generic failure in Settings, although the core explicitly knows locking is unavailable and retries cannot help until the browser context changes.
new_findings.evidence: src/lib/audit/device-key.ts:76-81 rejects before storage access; src/features/settings/AuditKeyCard.tsx:120-131 maps every non-unknown error to operationError='rotate', whose copy at lines 210-214 says 'Try Re-key again.' The unsupported test checks storage safety but not the user-facing recovery message.
new_findings.impact: No key/history mutation or receipt loss; the user may repeat a permanently unavailable operation.

coverage_notes: No stale imports or unused old history helpers remain in device-key.ts; grep shows production callers use the updated public functions.

No nested lock acquisition: rotate and first-use paths call only unlocked internal helpers while holding the lock; receipt creation obtains the active key, and later rotations promote its pending history entry to retained history before that key can be hidden.

Prepared history entries remain hidden unless their id is active. If a history write commits then rejects, a pending orphan can remain in storage, but it is invisible to verification/history and does not displace the active key; no cleanup is present.

The overlap test uses independently imported modules, isolated storage, forced active-write barriers, and real Ed25519 signatures. It uses native Node Web Locks when available and a serialized dependency double otherwise; neither proves actual Chrome extension service-worker/page origin coordination. The separate native Settings lane must establish that.
The UI unknown-outcome test exercises the Settings component with mocked device-key/storage boundaries; it establishes rendered state transitions, not native key storage or browser lock semantics.
